summary.prose: Story s9 moves the remaining 24 direct git, gh and shell call sites in 17 files onto the one tool registry, so every call is approved, signalled and recorded through callTool. The work first audits the replacement table against the live tool schemas and builds the few missing read-only git tools and inputs, then adds one git-calls helper module and flips the team policy, refresh, signoff, handoff, build-runner, validation, ignore-filter, corpus and identity sites to it, widening their consumers first so the tree stays green. It ends by moving 32 test files off the exec seam, deleting the old runners and seams, turning the forbidden-spawn scan into a failing build step, and running the full sweep once.

tasks.title: Audit every replacement row against the live tool input schemas
tasks.summary: For each site in the LLD's replacement table read the git or gh tool's input and output schema and record whether the op carries every option the site uses. Write the result as the first draft of section 5 of docs/plans/tool-registry-migration-record.md (site, tool, op, gap or none). The audit covers all rows, not only the known gaps (git_diff_tree, git_merge_tree, git_hash_object type, git_rev_parse gitPath, git_status path filter, the diff name-only forms), and settles how each site that needs a path list gets it. The gap list it produces is final.
acceptanceChecks: a table with one row per site names its tool and op and says 'covered' or names the missing input
every gap is either in the list of tools t2 builds or is covered by deriving the value from an existing result, with the reason
the audit is checked by reading the tool definitions, not from memory
the gap list is stated as final; any gap beyond the four known additions becomes a further task inserted before t3 by a plan amendment, not growth of t2

Existing calls of these tools are unchanged. Gaps beyond these four found by t1 are separate tasks, not part of t2.
